census.bucket: Wind — All wind electricity generation formats plus wind-asset life extension and circularity (Clean Energy Supply)

variations.name: Onshore utility-scale turbines
variations.description: Large three-blade horizontal-axis turbines (3-8+ MW) on land farms convert bulk wind into grid electricity and are among the cheapest sources of new generation worldwide; ~117 GW was installed globally in 2025 alone.

companies.name: Vestas
companies.what: World's largest turbine OEM by cumulative installs with the EnVentus onshore platform and the industry's biggest global service fleet.
companies.signal: First OEM to pass 200 GW cumulative installed (2025); 12.9 GW installed outside China in 2025 and ~16 GW firm orders.

companies.name: Goldwind
companies.what: China's top OEM and pioneer of direct-drive permanent-magnet onshore turbines at massive domestic scale.
companies.signal: World #1 annual installer in 2025 with 29.7 GW installed in China; 163 GW cumulative (global #2).

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.what: US onshore leader running a simplified 'workhorse product' strategy (2.8/3.6 MW platforms) plus a large repowering franchise.
companies.signal: 5.8 GW installed outside China in 2025; together with Vestas holds ~93% of the US market; 125 GW cumulative.

companies.name: Siemens Gamesa
companies.what: Top-3 Western OEM rebuilding its onshore business after the 4.X/5.X platform quality crisis while keeping offshore leadership.
companies.signal: 148 GW cumulative installed; 5.4 GW installed outside China in 2025.

companies.name: Envision Energy
companies.what: Chinese 'smart turbine' OEM that couples wind with storage and green-hydrogen industrial parks.
companies.signal: Passed 100 GW cumulative (103 GW) in 2025; 21.8 GW installed in China plus 4.2 GW internationally that year.

companies.name: Nordex Group
companies.what: German mid-market OEM focused on onshore turbines for Europe, Türkiye and Latin America.
companies.signal: Europe's #1 supplier in 2025 (7.7 GW installed ex-China); record ~10 GW order book.

companies.name: Mingyang Smart Energy
companies.what: Chinese OEM pushing the largest rotors in the industry and expanding aggressively outside China.
companies.signal: 18.6 GW installed in China in 2025 (global top-5 annual installer).

companies.name: Enercon
companies.what: German specialist in gearless direct-drive onshore turbines with a deep EU installed base.
companies.signal: Among the five largest suppliers in the EU in 2025.

companies.name: Suzlon
companies.what: India's largest wind OEM, recovered from debt restructuring to a record domestic order book.
companies.signal: Top-15 global OEM; dominant share of India's fast-growing onshore market.

variations.name: Fixed-bottom offshore wind (incl. foundations & installation tech)
variations.description: Turbines of 11-20 MW mounted on monopile or jacket foundations in waters under ~60 m capture stronger, steadier sea winds; a specialized chain of foundation fabricators and jack-up installation vessels is as decisive as the turbines themselves.

companies.name: Siemens Gamesa
companies.what: Offshore turbine market leader outside China with the SG 14-236 direct-drive platform.
companies.signal: Supplying Revolution Wind (first power Mar 2026), Sunrise Wind (84x11 MW) and Borkum Riffgrund 3 in 2025-26.

companies.name: Vestas
companies.what: Offshore challenger whose V236-15.0 MW flagship is entering serial deployment on European projects.
companies.signal: Multi-GW offshore backlog; among five OEMs above 100 GW cumulative (all segments).

companies.name: Ming Yang Smart Energy
companies.what: Builds the world's largest offshore turbines (MySE 18-20 MW class) and dominates Chinese offshore installations.
companies.signal: Global top-5 installer 2025; 18-20 MW typhoon-class machines commissioned in China.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.what: Haliade-X pioneer (13-15.5 MW) now shrinking offshore wind to one workhorse model and running off its backlog rather than seeking new orders.
companies.signal: Abandoned its 18 MW model, triggering cancellation of three New York projects; offshore unit posting losses.

companies.name: Ørsted
companies.what: World's largest offshore wind developer-operator; builds and owns fixed-bottom farms across Europe, Asia and the US.
companies.signal: Revolution Wind delivered first power to New England in Mar 2026 after surviving a federal stop-work order; completed ~DKK 60B rights issue in 2025 after US writedowns.

companies.name: Cadeler
companies.what: Operates the world's largest fleet of jack-up wind installation vessels handling both turbines and XXL monopile foundations.
companies.signal: Nine-plus vessel fleet incl. new A-class carrying six XXL monopile sets per trip; ~EUR 500M full-scope T&I contracts signed Nov 2025.

companies.name: Sif Group
companies.what: Dutch monopile fabricator supplying XXL foundations from its Rotterdam Maasvlakte 2 plant.
companies.signal: ~$450M expansion lifted capacity to ~500 kt/yr with robotic welding; 176 kt produced in 2025.

companies.name: EEW Group
companies.what: German manufacturer of XXL monopiles and transition pieces for North Sea and US projects.
companies.signal: Completed Nordlicht I monopiles ahead of schedule (2025); Sumitomo partnership to secure heavy steel plate.

companies.name: Havfram
companies.what: Norwegian wind-installation newcomer that ordered fourth-generation WTIV newbuilds.
companies.signal: Acquired by DEME in 2025 along with its two newbuild vessels.

companies.name: DEME Offshore
companies.what: Belgian marine contractor installing foundations, cables and turbines across global offshore wind markets.
companies.signal: Reported steady 2025 offshore wind activity and expanded turbine-installation capacity via the Havfram acquisition.

variations.name: Floating offshore wind platforms & mooring systems
variations.description: Turbines mounted on moored buoyant platforms (spar, semi-submersible, barge, TLP) unlock deep-water sites (>60 m) that hold most of the offshore wind resource near Japan, Korea, California and the Mediterranean; cost is still ~2-3x fixed-bottom.

companies.name: Equinor
companies.what: Hywind spar pioneer operating the world's first and largest floating wind farms.
companies.signal: Hywind Scotland (30 MW, since 2017) and Hywind Tampen (88 MW, powering North Sea oil platforms) both operating.

companies.name: Principle Power
companies.what: WindFloat semi-submersible platform used on the WindFloat Atlantic (25 MW) and Kincardine (50 MW) arrays.
companies.signal: ~105 MW of operating projects use its platform — the most of any independent floater designer; new CEO appointed 2025.

companies.name: BW Ideol
companies.what: Damping-pool barge floater in steel or concrete, proven on Floatgen (France) and Hibiki (Japan) demonstrators since 2018.
companies.signal: EUR 126M in EU Innovation Fund + French state grants (Mar 2026) for the Fos3F serial concrete-foundation factory; DNV basic design cert for 15 MW barge; Holcim took an equity stake.

companies.name: Stiesdal Offshore
companies.what: Industrialized, factory-built modular TetraSpar/TetraSub floaters designed by wind pioneer Henrik Stiesdal for mass production.
companies.signal: TetraSpar demonstrator (3.6 MW) operating off Norway since 2021; commercial team expanded 2025.

companies.name: Gazelle Wind Power
companies.what: Hinged low-draft platform with a dynamic mooring/counterweight system that cuts steel mass and port-depth requirements.
companies.signal: Raised an additional EUR 2M (May 2025) toward its 2 MW Nau Azul demonstrator off Portugal.

companies.name: Aikido Technologies
companies.what: Fold-flat floating platform assembled quayside in ~40 hours and towed out without heavy-lift vessels; also proposing turbine-integrated offshore AI data centers (AO60DC).
companies.signal: $4M seed round; US pilot platform demonstrated 10x faster assembly claim.

companies.name: X1 Wind
companies.what: Downwind, weathervaning PivotBuoy platform on a single-point TLP mooring that minimizes steel and seabed footprint.
companies.signal: X30 prototype delivered power off the Canary Islands; leading EU NextFloat 6 MW demo project.

companies.name: Marine Power Systems
companies.what: Welsh developer of the PelaFlex tension-leg floating wind platform, evolved from wave-energy technology.
companies.signal: GBP 8M Welsh Government investment (Mar 2026) to commercialize PelaFlex; ~$21.6M raised in total.

companies.name: Ming Yang Smart Energy
companies.what: Built OceanX, a twin-rotor V-shaped floating platform (16.6 MW combined) — the largest single floating wind unit installed — plus typhoon-class floating demos in China.
companies.signal: OceanX installed off Guangdong in 2024; multiple Chinese floating demonstrators delivered.

variations.white_space: Many platform designers but almost no commercial-scale buyers yet: LCOE is still ~2-3x fixed-bottom and ports, dynamic cables, moorings and serial fabrication are the bottleneck — the EUR 126M bet on BW Ideol's foundation factory shows the opening is industrialized floater/mooring manufacturing and anchor/mooring supply chains rather than yet another platform geometry.

variations.name: Airborne wind energy (kites, tethered drones)
variations.description: Tethered kites, rigid wings or drone-craft harvest the stronger, steadier winds at 200-800 m altitude using ~90% less material than a tower turbine, generating power via a ground winch (yo-yo cycle) or onboard rotors — attractive for off-grid, island and mobile uses.

companies.name: SkySails Power
companies.what: Soft-kite ground-generation systems (100-200 kW); the closest to serial sales with its new 'Kyo' unit.
companies.signal: Deployed Asia's first kite AWE system in Taiwan (Jul 2025) with partner AiSails; ENGIE joint pilot in Germany; official start of sales announced.

companies.name: Kitepower
companies.what: TU Delft spin-off making the 100 kW 'Falcon' mobile kite system for microgrids, islands and defense.
companies.signal: Operating pilots in the Caribbean (Aruba) and at RWE's consented Mayo, Ireland demonstration site.

companies.name: Kitemill
companies.what: Norwegian rigid-wing VTOL kite with ground generation; KM2 has a 16 m wingspan producing ~100 kW average.
companies.signal: EUR 3.35M EU Innovation Fund award for the 12-system NAWEP array; targeting 24-hour autonomous and multi-device operation from 2025.

companies.name: EnerKite
companies.what: German swept rigid-wing ground-gen system (EK200, 100 kW) aimed at farms and off-grid industry.
companies.signal: EUR 1.6M raised Nov 2025 toward Series A via crowd/angel financing; ~$1.85M total disclosed.

companies.name: Kitekraft
companies.what: Munich startup flying a tethered electric multicopter kite with onboard generation (fly-gen), a miniature heir to Makani's concept.
companies.signal: Sub-100 kW prototypes in flight testing; seed-stage.

companies.name: Windlift
companies.what: US maker of portable fly-gen 'airborne power systems' targeting defense and expeditionary power.
companies.signal: DoD development contracts; crowdfunding on Wefunder in 2025 at ~$34M valuation.

companies.name: Makani Power
companies.what: Pioneered the 600 kW M600 fly-gen energy kite under Google X/Alphabet.
companies.signal: Shut down by Alphabet in Feb 2020 after ~13 years; technology open-sourced — the sector's defining failure.

companies.name: Ampyx Power
companies.what: Dutch fixed-wing ground-gen developer (AP3 aircraft) once the sector's best-funded player.
companies.signal: Declared bankrupt after raising ~EUR 50M against an estimated EUR 500M development need; concept continued by successor Mozaero.

companies.name: TwingTec
companies.what: Swiss 'energy drone' ground-gen developer spun out of Empa/EPFL.
companies.signal: Listed among only ~8 surviving AWE players (down from 22 in 2017); little public activity since 2023.

variations.white_space: The field consolidated from ~22 players (2017) to ~8 after Makani and Ampyx proved utility-scale AWE needs hundreds of millions that single-digit-MW unit economics cannot yet justify; the credible near-term opening is 100-500 kW mobile/off-grid systems competing with diesel on islands, mines and defense sites, with autonomy and tether reliability as the gating technologies.

variations.name: Small & distributed wind (rooftop, ducted/shrouded)
variations.description: Turbines from sub-kW micro units to ~100 kW serve homes, farms, telecom towers and buildings on-site — valuable where grid power is expensive or absent — though cheap solar has pushed the segment into off-grid and hybrid niches.

companies.name: Bergey Windpower
companies.what: Battle-proven 1-15 kW residential and farm HAWTs with decades-long track record.
companies.signal: 35,000+ turbines installed across 120 countries; 2024 DOE award to upgrade blade manufacturing.

companies.name: Ryse Energy
companies.what: Abu Dhabi-based integrator of small wind and hybrid wind-solar-storage systems for off-grid telecom, oil & gas and rural electrification.
companies.signal: Acquired US micro-wind maker Primus Wind Power; installations across 70+ countries.

companies.name: Eocycle
companies.what: Canadian-Belgian maker of 25-100 kW direct-drive farm-scale turbines; consolidated the segment by absorbing XANT, Orenda and United Wind assets.
companies.signal: Transatlantic product line (EO/S-series) actively marketed; the segment's main roll-up.

companies.name: Primus Wind Power
companies.what: Air-series micro turbines (40-160 W class) for off-grid, marine and telecom power, among the most-sold wind products ever.
companies.signal: Hundreds of thousands of units shipped; acquired by Ryse Energy.

companies.name: Aeromine Technologies
companies.what: Motionless rooftop wind units that use building-edge aerodynamics to amplify airflow through an internal rotor, pitched as solar's rooftop companion.
companies.signal: $9M Series A (May 2024); pilots with BASF and commercial building owners.

companies.name: Flower Turbines
companies.what: Tulip-shaped quiet small VAWTs that perform better in clusters ('bouquet effect') for urban and commercial sites.
companies.signal: >$17M raised from 8,000+ crowd investors; launched Project Series 1 (2025) to finance commercial installations.

companies.name: United Wind
companies.what: Pioneered no-money-down residential wind leasing (WindLease) in the US before folding.
companies.signal: Ceased independent operations; assets acquired by Eocycle.

companies.name: XZERES Wind
companies.what: Once-prominent Oregon maker of 2.4-10 kW residential turbines that collapsed after years of losses.
companies.signal: Effectively exited the market after financial distress in the early 2020s; brand assets changed hands.

variations.white_space: Solar-PV's cost collapse hollowed out small wind — economics rarely close on-grid, urban rooftop wind has a long failure record (turbulence, low hub-height speeds), and the sector's history is bankruptcies and roll-ups; the openings are hybrid wind+solar+storage off-grid kits for telecom/islands/defense, and building-integrated designs with independently validated yields like Aeromine's.

variations.name: Vertical-axis & novel rotor designs (incl. bladeless/oscillating)
variations.description: Alternative architectures — vertical-axis rotors, bladeless oscillating masts, track-mounted wings, multi- and single-rotor floaters — trade the mature three-blade format for lower height, lower center of gravity, denser packing or cheaper manufacture.

companies.name: SeaTwirl
companies.what: Swedish floating spar VAWT whose low center of gravity suits deep-water floating duty; Nasdaq First North-listed.
companies.signal: EUR 15M Horizon Europe 'Verti-Go' award (Sep 2025) to build and operate a 2 MW floating VAWT demonstrator; design phase began Oct 2025.

companies.name: World Wide Wind
companies.what: Norwegian contra-rotating, tilting floating VAWT concept claimed scalable to 40 MW per unit.
companies.signal: Partnership with aluminum giant Hydro for tower materials; small-scale prototype testing in Norway.

companies.name: Airloom Energy
companies.what: Wing-cars circulating on a low oval trackway (~25 m high) to deliver utility-scale power with far less steel, height and radar profile than a tower turbine.
companies.signal: $13.75M financing (Oct 2024) backed by Breakthrough Energy/Lowercarbon; broke ground on Wyoming utility-scale pilot Jun 2025, power expected late 2025 and commercial demos in 2027.

companies.name: XFlow Energy
companies.what: Seattle-area maker of a 30 kW low-maintenance VAWT (XFE-13) engineered with NREL/DOE support for distributed sites.
companies.signal: DOE Competitiveness Improvement Project awardee; first commercial units in field testing.

companies.name: Vortex Bladeless
companies.what: Spanish bladeless mast that oscillates via vortex-induced vibration to make micro-power with no rotating parts.
companies.signal: More than a decade in development with heavy press but minimal verified commercial deployment.

companies.name: Alpha 311
companies.what: UK startup mounting small VAWTs on roadside lampposts to harvest vehicle-induced airflow.
companies.signal: Down to 1 employee at end-2024 ($2.61M raised); Southampton wind-tunnel testing reported in 2025 — barely alive.

companies.name: TouchWind
companies.what: Dutch one-piece tilting single-rotor floating turbine designed to survive typhoons and slash manufacturing cost.
companies.signal: Investment from Mitsui O.S.K. Lines; scaled-model testing — full-scale demo not yet verified.

variations.white_space: Decades of VAWT failures (lower aerodynamic efficiency, fatigue cycling) plus the 40-year cost/reliability learning curve of three-blade HAWTs make head-on competition near-hopeless; credible openings exist only where the HAWT form factor itself fails — floating offshore (low center of gravity: SeaTwirl, World Wide Wind), height/radar-restricted land (Airloom, which is the segment's only well-funded utility-scale bet), and harsh-weather niches.

variations.name: Wind repowering, blade recycling & life extension
variations.description: Replacing or upgrading aging turbines on existing permitted sites (repowering), recycling decommissioned fiberglass blades into new materials, and using robots, drones and predictive analytics to stretch asset life — keeping the existing fleet productive and circular as ~hundreds of GW age past year 15.

companies.name: NextEra Energy Resources
companies.what: Largest US renewables owner running the biggest fleet-scale wind repowering program.
companies.signal: Target raised to ~1.9 GW repowered through 2026 at 50-80% of new-build cost while restarting 10-year PTCs.

companies.name: RWE
companies.what: European utility repowering aging farms across Spain, Germany and Texas.
companies.signal: Forest Creek, TX: 54 old Siemens Gamesa units replaced by 45 new GE Vernova turbines adding ~30 years of life; Muel (Spain) repowering started Apr 2025.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.what: Sells OEM repowering packages (new rotors/nacelles on existing foundations) for the large aging US fleet.
companies.signal: Booked 1.1 GW of US onshore repowering orders in 2025, with CODs in 2026-27.

companies.name: Veolia
companies.what: Shreds decommissioned blades for cement-kiln co-processing (fuel plus raw material) at its Missouri facility.
companies.signal: Master agreement with GE since 2020; among the named leaders in the 2025 blade-recycling market report.

companies.name: Carbon Rivers
companies.what: Pyrolysis process recovering 99.9%-purity glass fiber from blades for reuse in new composites.
companies.signal: DOE-supported; thousands of tonnes processed and a ~50,000 t/yr Knoxville facility in build-out.

companies.name: REGEN Fiber
companies.what: Mechanical blade recycling into fiber reinforcement additives for concrete and asphalt (Alliant Energy/Travero subsidiary).
companies.signal: Iowa plant running at ~60 million lb/yr capacity, one of the few commercially operational recycling routes in 2025.

companies.name: Continuum
companies.what: Mechanically separates blades into fiber/resin/metal streams and remanufactures them into composite building panels.
companies.signal: First factory in Esbjerg, Denmark operational; six European factories planned incl. UK.

companies.name: Global Fiberglass Solutions
companies.what: Early blade-to-pellet recycler (EcoPoly) that became notorious for stockpiled, unprocessed blades in Texas and Iowa.
companies.signal: Still cited in market reports but with little verifiable processing activity — a cautionary tale on recycling economics.

companies.name: Aerones
companies.what: Robotic in-situ blade inspection and repair (leading-edge erosion, lightning-protection testing) that avoids cranes and rope teams.
companies.signal: $62M oversubscribed round (Jun 2025, Activate Capital/S2G); revenue nearly tripled YoY; new Dallas US hub.

companies.name: SkySpecs
companies.what: Autonomous drone blade inspections feeding the Horizon asset-health platform — the industry's largest blade-damage dataset.
companies.signal: $20M raised Mar 2025 (~$140M total, Series E); 270,000+ turbines inspected for 125 customers in 19 countries.
